answer.short:
$S=4\pi r^2$.

The pyramid volumes sum to $\frac13rS$, which equals the sphere volume $\frac43\pi r^3$.
answer.worked:
Let $S$ be the surface area of the sphere. The small base areas together make up $S$. In the very-small-pyramid model, each pyramid has height $r$, so their total volume is $\frac13rS$.

This equals the volume of the sphere:
$$\begin{align*}
\frac13rS&=\frac43\pi r^3\\
rS&=4\pi r^3\\
S&=4\pi r^2.
\end{align*}$$
